outcome: number of analgesic doses required in 48 hours
waking up at night due to pain
cohort: 104 females undergoing elective or emergency caesarean section (ASA Grade I and II) at R D Gardi Medical College, Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, India.
finding: Rectal diclofenac suppository was more effective for postoperative pain relief after caesarean section than rectal glycerine, resulting in a longer time to first analgesic dose, fewer analgesic doses required over 48 hours, and fewer patients waking up at night due to pain.
